dedupe_keys.name: backbone energy network optimisation framework vtt gams

description: Backbone is an energy systems modelling framework written in GAMS and developed by VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland with University College Dublin, according to the G-PST Open Tools Portal. The README describes it as a generic energy network optimisation tool covering generation, storage, transmission and conversion between energy carriers; operation and investment; energy, emissions, materials and costs; forecasts and reserves; and hydropower reservoirs, cascades and delays. Coverage: any energy sector at a chosen level of detail; the README lists applications in multi-sector studies (power, district heating, transport, buildings, industry), electricity distribution grids, building heating, resource supply, power-to-X and life-cycle emissions. The portal adds that it runs as an investment model (single or multi-period, myopic or full foresight) or as a rolling unit commitment model, with stochastic parameters, multiple reserve products, start-up trajectories, storage and DC power flow, and lets the time step length change along the horizon. Format and access: source code and wiki on the VTT GitLab server; the repository showed activity on 28 September 2026. Licence: GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0 or later (portal). Caveats: a GAMS licence and solver are needed to run it; the wiki pages beyond the home page were not read. Simulation uses: capacity expansion and operational dispatch studies of coupled power, heat and gas systems, including hydropower cascades. Related records: SpineOpt (model-spineopt) is another open energy system optimisation framework listed in the same portal category.
